title: Shannon Entropy as an Order Parameter for the Two-Dimensional Confined Coulomb Systems: Exact Balance Law, Topological Charge Sum Rule, and Boundary Saturation
authors: Goergiy K. Lavrov, Eduard G. Nikonov
abstract: We establish a complete information-theoretic framework for the known minimum-energy configurations of the two-dimensional Thomson problem on a hard-wall disk, based on the Shannon entropy of the Voronoi topological charge distribution. Two exact results are proven and hold for all studied systems of size $N=12$--$10^5$. First, an entropy balance law decomposes the total entropy into bulk, boundary, and mixing contributions without approximation. Second, a topological charge sum rule fixes the total charge at twice the number of boundary particles plus six; together with the observed separation of bulk and boundary coordination numbers, it yields exact relations between the populations of three- and four-coordinated boundary particles and the bulk charge. We further prove that the boundary entropy is bounded by the binary maximum and that saturation of this bound is equivalent to the bulk charge per boundary particle approaching minus one half, a regime that the framework itself restricts to boundaries of at least twelve particles. All identities are verified numerically to machine precision, locating bulk nucleation at $56$ particles, the maximum of global disorder at $146$, and the onset of boundary saturation beyond about $1000$. The framework carries over to closed spherical geometry, where the total charge is fixed at twelve.
summary: This paper develops an exact information-theoretic framework using Shannon entropy to analyze the minimum-energy states of 2D confined Coulomb systems. Key results include an entropy balance law and a topological charge sum rule that precisely constrain the system's structure. This work establishes deep mathematical connections between statistical mechanics, topology, and information theory in classical many-body systems.
main_problem: To establish a complete, exact information-theoretic framework linking the topological complexity of minimum-energy configurations in 2D confined Coulomb systems to measurable quantities.
main_result: The authors prove an entropy balance law and a topological charge sum rule, yielding exact relations between boundary and bulk particle populations.
method: The analysis uses Shannon entropy decomposition, topological arguments (Voronoi tessellation), and rigorous mathematical proofs applied to numerically verified minimum-energy configurations.
model_or_system: The system consists of $N$ identical point charges interacting via the $1/r$ Coulomb potential, confined within a two-dimensional disk by a hard-wall potential.
key_observables: Total, bulk, boundary, and mixing Shannon entropies ($H_{total}, H_{bulk}, H_{edge}, H_{mix}$); Topological charge sum ($\sum q_i$); Coordination number populations ($n_3, n_4$).
important_parameters: System size $N$ ($12$ to $10^5$); Boundary particle count $N_E$; Bulk charge density $Q_B/N_E$.
main_assumptions: The derived identities apply to local minima satisfying topological conditions; the core results rely on two empirical inputs (Observations III.1 and III.2) specific to Coulomb minima.
figures_summary: The notes indicate the presence of figures showing the evolution of entropy components ($H_{total}, H_{bulk}, H_{edge}, H_{mix}$) versus system size $N$, and tables presenting systematic numerical data across varying parameters.
paper_structure: The paper develops the framework by first defining the system and entropy components, then proving the Entropy Balance Law and the Topological Charge Sum Rule, followed by deriving constraints on boundary/bulk populations, and concluding with the analysis of boundary entropy saturation.
why_interesting: The use of information theory (Shannon entropy) as a rigorous order parameter to characterize the equilibrium structure of classical interacting particle systems provides a powerful, generalizable mathematical tool for condensed matter physics.
